memory_update.text: CECO should be retained for later Serenity layers as an underfollowed gas-power emissions/exhaust-system candidate; key survival test is backlog mix and margin conversion from natural-gas power projects.

Woodward should be retained as a controls/component supplier hypothesis for gas turbines and reciprocating engines; later layers must quantify Industrial segment exposure to power generation and aftermarket revenue.

GE Vernova confirms the node’s reference bottleneck: turbine backlog, slot reservations, installed gas-turbine base, and services capacity are central indicators for the dispatchable-generation power-island funnel.

Need another pass for US-listed speculative or micro/small-cap reciprocating-engine packagers, generator rental/service networks, load-bank testing, turbine repair tooling, specialty castings/forgings, and control-system software vendors.

node: Gas turbines, turbine services, reciprocating engines, backup generation, and power-island equipment
summary: Layer 1B expands this node with one reference leader and two second-order suppliers. The reference lane confirms that gas-turbine OEM capacity, slot reservations, installed-base services, and long-cycle power equipment are now explicit chokepoints. The underfollowed lane shifts attention away from only turbine OEMs toward emissions/exhaust systems and precision controls used on gas turbines, steam turbines, compressors, and reciprocating engines. No buy/sell view is implied.
